memory_candidates.content: In this Lean repository, TaskFrame.reflection is the unguarded reflection law and its proof opens with a classical eq_or_ne d 0, so any proof that rewrites with it measures Classical.choice. TaskFrame.reflection_of_ne (the off-zero wrapper) does not. Any mixed-orientation task-relation rewrite whose case is strict can therefore be made choice-free by supplying a `d - d' != 0` side condition via sub_ne_zero.mpr and rewriting with reflection_of_ne instead. This has now been the decisive repair three times on independent fronts (PlusLanguage.paste_rel, Presheaf.glue_rel in the Sheaf clause, and Presheaf.Ray.seamGlue_rel), each time turning [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] into [propext, Quot.sound] with a three-line substitution. The diagnostic is that the clean/dirty boundary sits at the exact declaration performing the reflection rewrite, so #print axioms on the immediately preceding lemma localizes the leak in one step.

This repository's check-module-invariants.sh C23 forbids outer-shadows-inner BASE-name pairs regardless of namespace: its dead-declaration census keys on the last dot-segment, so two declarations sharing a base name mask each other and neither can ever be reported dead. Putting a colliding declaration in a sub-namespace (e.g. Presheaf.Ray.glue beside Presheaf.glue) therefore does NOT satisfy the gate -- the base name itself must differ. Plan when promoting a probe into a cluster that already owns the obvious name: pick a distinct base name up front (seamGlue beside glue) rather than discovering the collision after the module is written and a 17-minute rebuild has already run.

Promoting an evidence probe into FormalSystem/ in this repository hits three gate constraints that probes themselves never see, because probes are compiled by `lake env lean` outside the library's leanOptions: (1) the mathlibStandardSet linters apply, and linter.style.show rejects the `show` tactic -- use `change` where the goal changes, per scripts/warning-budget.txt's own disposition note; (2) `ring` and `linarith` are unavailable in the Presheaf/PlusLanguage import closures, so `by push_cast; ring` side goals must become `by push_cast; omega`; (3) C28 reads warnings from the LAST BUILD, not from the working tree, so a --no-build gate run reports stale warning counts after a fix. Verify a promoted module with `lake env lean -Dlinter.mathlibStandardSet=true -DautoImplicit=false <file>` before trusting a gate run.

In this repository FormalSystem/Semantics.lean imports the Semantics/Presheaf aggregator, and Semantics.lean is upstream of essentially the whole Metalogic tree. Consequence: ANY edit to a module under FormalSystem/Semantics/Presheaf/ -- including a docstring-only edit -- forces a near-full ~2800-job rebuild taking roughly 17 minutes. Two practical rules follow. Never start a guarded build until a phase's edits are final, because a build started mid-edit yields a verdict for the wrong source and must be discarded. And batch docstring/prose polish for a Presheaf module into the same pre-build edit window as its proofs.

docs/reference/paper-definitions-of-record.md distinguishes two states that are easy to conflate: a DANGLING KNOWN-ANCHORS row (recorded, citable, resolves in the record) and 'deliberately NOT pinned' (absent from KNOWN-ANCHORS by a recorded maintenance-surface decision). Citing a deliberately-unpinned anchor from any FormalSystem/ docstring or README fails C15 with 'N paper-anchor citation(s) resolve to nothing'. def:path-category, def:conduche and cor:path-fibration are in the second state, not the first. When a plan instructs citing an anchor 'as a DANGLING row', verify against the record's KNOWN-ANCHORS block before writing it -- the alternative to naming it is to describe the result and its non-landed status without the label, which keeps the content and avoids widening a record the tree does not depend on.
